name: JiyongKim
why: Seoul menswear dyed by weather — garments tied and left outdoors for months so sun, wind and rain do the fading, on reconstructed vintage cloth.
origin: Jiyong Kim — Bunka in Tokyo, then Central Saint Martins; worked at Lemaire, at Louis Vuitton under Virgil Abloh, and at Maison Mihara Yasuhiro. The brand began when Tokyo's GR8 bought almost his entire thesis collection. LVMH Prize semi-finalist 2024. Founding year given variously as 2020 and 2021.
opview: Kim found the technique in Seoul's fabric markets — a trench coat left in the sun for months had faded into a pattern he had never seen, and he read it as beauty rather than damage. Each piece takes over a month.

onething.n: process is the signature, not one style; months outdoors. NO LINK — the SSENSE slug could not be verified and jiyong-kim was invented; brand styles itself one word. Stocked at SSENSE, MR PORTER, DSM, GR8, 10 Corso Como.

notes.weird: Weather does the dyeing. Tying cloth and leaving it outdoors for months is a process nobody else runs, and the results cannot be fully predicted.
notes.avant: Sun-bleaching as method rather than as finish. The avant-garde claim is in the making — a garment whose pattern is determined by months of weather is a different proposition from a difficult cut.

cities: No own US retail. Flagship Hannam-dong, Seoul (2025) — a quiet alley behind the Italian Embassy, not the main strip. Dover Street Market · MR PORTER · SSENSE · GR8 Tokyo · 10 Corso Como Seoul
